newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin rules out changes to Russian constitution.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin rules out changes to Russian constitution.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltisn said in his annual state of the nation address on Thursday he would not allow constitutional amendments demanded by the opposition to try to weaken his presidential powers.
"I am against such a hurry. First we have to learn to respect the constitution...and only after that think about changes," he said in a televised speech to parliament.
Yeltsin, 66, spoke clearly and confidently in his most important policy speech since he was elected for a four-year second term last July.

He has spent much of his second term fighting ill health, prompting the opposition communists to call for amendments to the 1993 constitution to water down Yeltsin's powers or to try to force him to resign for health reasons.
Yeltsin has made clear several times that he will not allow such changes, but his determined comments on Thursday underlined his intention to hold on to his vast powers under a constitution
